source_conflicts.resolution: Both readings sit at the low-to-moderate end of typical energy-sector through-cycle P/E ranges, so valuation_burden is not graded 'low' outright — per etf-grading-standards' cyclicals guidance (a cyclical sector's P/E can look cheapest right at an earnings-margin peak), the low P/E is treated as an ambiguous signal rather than confirmation of a discount, and graded B0 (ordinary) rather than A.

coverage.impact_of_missing: All six criteria were established for both sectors within the 3-4-search-per-sector budget; no criterion was left null. Confidence is capped at medium rather than high because: (1) two risk_overheat/flows_positioning citations for each sector rest on tertiary finance-content sites rather than primary/vendor data, (2) the XLE P/E figure conflicts across sources, and (3) some IT relative-strength and flows figures could not be pinned to an exact September 2026 as-of date and are treated as recent YTD approximations.

sectors.name: information technology
rationale: 01_market_regime.json names information technology directly in favorable_sector_types, citing record semiconductor sales (+104.1% YoY to $120.6B) and raised hyperscaler capex guidance (Alphabet $195-205B, TSMC $60-64B) — a direct, clearly-based macro_fit match (source_idx 0).
2026 US semiconductor earnings growth consensus is ~98% and hyperscaler capex guidance has been raised rather than cut, supporting a confirmed-upward earnings_momentum read (source_idx 0).
XLK has outperformed SPY YTD (+27.45% vs +8.10%) and over 10 years (25.40%/yr vs 15.53%/yr), a clear relative_strength edge, though the trend was mixed as recently as February 2026 (source_idx 1, 2).

XLK's P/E (33.02x) sits inside its own 5-year band [29.48, 36.41] rather than breaking above it, and roughly matches the broader S&P 500 IT sector P/E (32.88) — an ordinary rather than low or extreme valuation_burden (source_idx 3, 4).
Global tech-fund inflows hit a record +$131B YTD through mid-August 2026, more than doubling over the prior four months — a confirmed flows_positioning tailwind (source_idx 6).
risks_to_check: risk_overheat is the weakest criterion (C+): the semiconductor trade shows documented crowded institutional positioning and a prior sharp selloff after a +130% Philly Semi Index rally, and AI capex is now an estimated ~93% of hyperscaler operating cash flow per 01's key_risks — verify whether hyperscaler capex guidance holds through the next earnings cycle before treating IT strength as durable (source_idx 0, 7).

Verify the exact September 2026 XLK-vs-SPY performance gap directly (e.g., stockanalysis.com or Barchart) rather than relying on the YTD approximation used here, since the search did not return a September-dated snapshot (source_idx 2).

A confirmed or larger-than-expected Fed rate hike at the September 16, 2026 FOMC (01's key_risks: ~60-67% hike odds) would pressure IT's above-market valuation multiple disproportionately given its long-duration earnings profile.

sectors.name: energy & power
rationale: 01_market_regime.json names energy & power directly in favorable_sector_types, citing accelerating earnings consensus (+16.3% FY2026) and a structural AI-driven data-center power-demand tailwind (31GW to 66GW 2025-2027) alongside the oil-price surge — a direct, clearly-based macro_fit match (source_idx 0).

Energy-sector earnings growth consensus is accelerating sharply (71.0%/42.1%/40.9%/37.6% YoY across the next four quarters per 01), supporting a confirmed-upward earnings_momentum read, though natural-gas-weighted operators are flagged as a mixed pocket within the sector (source_idx 0).
XLE is up roughly +28-32% YTD in 2026 while SPY is close to flat, and energy is named the top-performing S&P 500 sector of 2026 — a clear relative_strength edge (source_idx 7).

XLE's P/E (reported as 13.04 or 17.61x depending on source) sits at the low-to-moderate end of typical energy multiples, but per the cyclicals guidance in etf-grading-standards a low P/E during a margin/earnings peak is an ambiguous rather than confirmatory 'cheap' signal, so valuation_burden is graded ordinary rather than low (source_idx 8).

Flows are genuinely mixed: XLE's 1-, 3-, and 6-month net flows are all negative (-$866M/-$2.29B/-$1.62B) even as the most recent 4-week average (+$1.0B) and 1-year figure (+$1.75B) are positive — graded neutral (source_idx 9).
risks_to_check: risk_overheat is the weakest criterion (C0): the rally is substantially built on a geopolitically-driven oil spike (US-Iran tensions), and the sector has already shown how fast that can reverse — a single ceasefire headline in April 2026 triggered a -$1.0B single-day XLE outflow, the largest in 14 years. Verify oil-price durability before treating current earnings momentum as structural rather than cyclical (source_idx 0, 8, 10).
Resolve the XLE P/E source conflict (13.04 vs 17.61x) against a primary/vendor filing-based figure before using it in any downstream ETF-level valuation call.

Any de-escalation of the Iran situation, an OPEC+ supply response, or a Fed rate hike (elevating the discount rate on capital-intensive energy infrastructure) are named directly in 01's key_risks as potential reversal triggers for this sector's earnings and price momentum alike.
